new_design_findings.counterexample: A future implementation checks a supplied authorizer and passes deny-all/missing-context tests, but accepts a foreign allow-all policy handle or caller-chosen privileged principal. Initial and exact replay may then succeed. This is a test-plan counterexample, not an executed I6 product defect.
new_design_findings.gap: R10 explicitly prohibits both substitutions, but T07/T26 do not enumerate these direct API attacks. Sender permission forgery and deny-all injection do not necessarily exercise context-origin validation.
new_design_findings.required_contract_change: No substantive R10/ADR change. Enumerate foreign-policy-handle and forged-principal negative cases in the implementation's T07/T26 mapping.
new_design_findings.rereview_condition: Frozen I6-A independently refuses both attacks before dependency lookups/writes and before replay duplicate success, records zero row delta/no denied existence disclosure, and demonstrates that the substituted policy service is not invoked as authority.
